title: Qualitative context-to-answer retrieval examples
subject: Representative distinctions and confusions from matched and natural conversations

examples.title: Earlier topic survives intervening turns
examples.lead: Shared final turn: “Could you recap your main advice in one sentence?”
lines: Hiking → route, weather, gear, and backup-plan advice.
Birthday → treasure hunt, crafts, games, and cake ideas.

examples.title: System constraint changes the answer
examples.lead: Shared final turn: “How is the stock market doing right now?”
lines: No internet → says current data are unavailable.
Browsing allowed → offers to look up an index.

examples.title: Related travel itineraries
examples.lead: Final user turn: “puedes darme un plan de viaje a El Calafate, de 6 dias ?”
lines: True answer → six-day Spanish itinerary for El Calafate.
Top confuser → Portuguese itinerary for the Alps.

examples.title: Different language tasks
examples.lead: Final user turn: Complete “I want to learn more about the American culture by”
lines: True answer → completes the requested sentence.
